clue.text: Plant's core cultivated with soil to reproduce

indicators.note: cultivated ground is turned over and worked, so the letters before and after it are dug into a new order

parts.note: the letters as written, the apostrophe dropped
taken as written

explanation.surface: A gardener mixes the heart of a plant into soil to propagate it.
explanation.definitionFit: Plants cross-pollinate when pollen passes from one to another, which is how they breed and make seed.

clue.text: What might make a full house from pack? Run following suit

definitions.text: What might make a full house

indicators.note: following means coming behind, so the run letter is placed after the word for suit

parts.note: to pack a place is to crowd it, and a pack of people is a crowd
to suit someone is to please them
R is the cricket scoring abbreviation for a run

explanation.surface: A card player pulls a full house from the pack, with a run following in the same suit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Following' puts the run after the suit word. The card-game words (full house, pack, suit, run) all have other jobs.
explanation.definitionFit: A popular act draws big audiences, so it is the sort of thing that sells out a theatre.

clue.text: Boris saving skin? He finally left Oxford college

indicators.note: keeping only what is under the skin means the outer letters of the name are peeled away

parts.note: the name without its first and last letters

indicators.note: finally points to the last letter of the word before it

parts.note: the final letter of the pronoun
L is the standard abbreviation for left

explanation.surface: A former Oxford student called Boris loses face and leaves the university.
explanation.definitionFit: Oriel is one of the colleges of Oxford University, on Oriel Square.

clue.text: It rains, empty sewage at sea, this might get dirt on surface

definitions.text: this might get dirt on surface

indicators.note: something at sea is adrift and confused, so the letters are tossed into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: an emptied word has lost its contents, keeping just its first and last letters

parts.note: only the outside letters of the word survive

explanation.surface: Rain washes raw sewage into the sea, leaving filth on the surface.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Get dirt' means to get at grime and kill germs, though the surface suggests it spreads dirt instead.
explanation.definitionFit: A sanitiser is a cleaning product used to kill germs on worktops and other surfaces.

clue.text: Did face set day after surgical procedure?

parts.note: OP is short for operation
to set a question or problem is to pose it
D is the standard abbreviation for day

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether a face-lift was booked for the day after an operation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'After' puts the operation first and the rest behind it.
explanation.definitionFit: Two teams that faced each other in a match opposed each other: both verbs mean met as rivals.

clue.text: Deal close to drug mule taking tablets in grams?

indicators.note: dealing cards scatters them around the table, so these letters are spread into a fresh order
the close of a word is its end, so only its final letter is used

parts.note: the final letter of the word
taken as written
E is slang for an ecstasy tablet, so several are Es

explanation.surface: A drug smuggler is caught carrying pills weighed out in grams.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Grams' looks like the weight of the drugs; it is the plural of gram, the name for chickpeas and similar pulses. The question mark flags a definition by example.
explanation.definitionFit: Gram is a name for several pulses such as chickpea and mung bean, all of them podded crops.

clue.text: New Year bill at the end paid for by plastic

parts.note: N is the standard abbreviation for new
Y is the standard abbreviation for year

indicators.note: the end of a word is its last letter, which is all that is used

parts.note: the final letter of the word
a round that is on someone is paid for by them, as in 'drinks are on me'

explanation.surface: The New Year credit-card bill finally lands, all of it paid on plastic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Plastic' looks like a credit card; it is the material.
explanation.definitionFit: Nylon is a synthetic polymer, one of the earliest man-made plastics used for fibres and moulded parts.

clue.text: Shortness of balls: second over at the crease

indicators.note: one thing set at the middle of another is placed within it, so one piece sits inside the other

parts.note: balls is slang for testicles, whose formal plural is this word
a batter at the crease in cricket is in, that is, batting
S is the standard abbreviation for second

explanation.surface: A cricket commentator remarks on balls bowled at the crease in the second over.
explanation.walkthrough: The cricket scene hides the anatomy: balls are the body parts. 'Over' follows the second, which comes last.
explanation.definitionFit: Being short with someone means being curt and irritable, the quality of testiness.

clue.text: Bulb repeatedly lit with current suppressed

indicators.note: something suppressed is held down and kept in, so one piece is enclosed by the other

parts.note: a light that is lit is on, and repeatedly doubles it
I is the physics symbol for electric current

explanation.surface: A light bulb keeps switching on, though the current is turned down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bulb' sounds electrical alongside lit and current, but it is the vegetable.
explanation.definitionFit: An onion is the swollen underground bulb of a plant of the allium family, eaten as a vegetable.

clue.text: Fighter turning up to register after soldier

indicators.note: after sends the register word behind the soldier word, reversing the order they are printed in
turning something round makes it face the other way, so the short word is read backwards

parts.note: taken as written before it turns
GI is an American soldier
a register is a list of names

explanation.surface: A boxer shows up to sign on with the army register after a soldier.
explanation.definitionFit: A pugilist is a boxer, someone who fights with the fists.

clue.text: Meeting sweethearts — they're easy to take out

parts.note: a sitting is a meeting of a council or court
duck is a British term of endearment, like love or dear

explanation.surface: A meeting of sweethearts, the kind of people easy to ask out on a date.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Take out' suggests a date; it means shoot down. Duck as an endearment is chiefly northern English and Midlands.
explanation.definitionFit: A sitting duck is an easy target, someone simple to attack or eliminate.

clue.text: Strange US diet — belly of fella gets thinner

indicators.note: strange means odd and out of order, so these letters are shuffled into another arrangement

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: the belly is the middle of the body, so the central letter of the word is taken

parts.note: the central letter of the five

explanation.surface: On an odd American diet a man's paunch slims down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gets thinner' reads as losing weight, but it means watering down.
explanation.definitionFit: To dilute a liquid is to add water so it becomes weaker and less concentrated.

clue.text: Revealing outfit? Mini skirts a new look, ultimately

indicators.note: to skirt something is to go round its edge, so the outer word surrounds the others

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
N is the standard abbreviation for new

indicators.note: ultimately means in the end, so just the last letter of the word before it

parts.note: the final letter of the word

explanation.surface: Fashion talk: mini skirts are giving a new look, an outfit that reveals a lot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Skirts' reads as the garments, but it is the verb meaning goes round.
explanation.definitionFit: A mankini is a skimpy one-piece men's swimsuit, famously worn in Borat, which covers very little.

clue.text: Both ends of laces threaded by feeling holes

indicators.note: a thread passing through something runs inside it, so one piece goes between the others
both ends of a word are its first and last letters, which are kept

parts.note: just the first and last letters
an air is a feeling or impression, as in an air of mystery

explanation.surface: Shoelaces are fed by touch through the eyelet holes.
explanation.walkthrough: The shoelace picture makes 'holes' sound like eyelets; here it means animals' dens.
explanation.definitionFit: A lair is a wild animal's den, and a hole is a burrow or hiding place, so the plurals match.

clue.text: I learn it off by heart, essentially with other things

indicators.note: something gone off has turned bad and out of order, so the letters before it are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: the essence of a word is its core, so the central letter is taken

parts.note: the central letter of the five

explanation.surface: A student says they learn their lines off by heart, along with other things.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Off by heart' reads as one idiom, but it splits into the shuffle signal and the source of one letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Inter alia is Latin for among other things, used to show that a list is not complete.

clue.text: In case of doubt, is your husband inside cheating?

indicators.note: inside places the pieces before it within the case letters
the case of a word is its outside, so just its first and last letters

parts.note: the first and last letters only
taken as written
H is the standard abbreviation for husband
one's means your in the general sense, as in 'one does one's best'

explanation.surface: A suspicious wife asks whether her husband is being unfaithful at home.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone cheating is acting dishonestly, deceiving others for gain.

clue.text: Have more than admired dress? Exposed on top

indicators.note: in a down entry the piece on top comes first, so the exposed word is written above the dress word

parts.note: something exposed is out in the open
a number is an eye-catching outfit, as in a little black number

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether to show off a much-admired dress that is revealing up top.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On top' puts the exposed piece first in a down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: To outnumber a group is to exceed it in count, being more numerous than it.

clue.text: Wake wanting bit of medicine at hospital

parts.note: to be after something is to want it

indicators.note: a bit of a word here is its opening letter

parts.note: the first letter of the word
taken as written
H is the standard abbreviation for hospital

explanation.surface: A patient wakes needing a dose of medicine in hospital.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wake' looks like a verb, but it is the noun, as in the wake of a storm.
explanation.definitionFit: The wake of an event is what follows it, the consequences or period after it.

clue.text: A sequence of four letters about one native

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: about means around, so the outer piece goes around the one after it

parts.note: four consecutive letters of the alphabet, chosen to fit
an is the indefinite article, meaning one

explanation.surface: A local person writes four letters in a row around the figure one.
explanation.walkthrough: The four letters are not named, so crossing letters are needed to pick them.
explanation.definitionFit: An Afghani is a native of Afghanistan, though the word is also that country's currency.

clue.text: Online reference needing number and name

parts.note: the # sign is called hash in Britain and number sign in the US
a tag is a label or name

explanation.surface: A web citation asks for a phone number and a name.
explanation.definitionFit: A hashtag is a word preceded by the # sign used on social media to label and find posts on a topic.

clue.text: Boxer knocking the stuffing out of Teddy boy

indicators.note: knocking out the stuffing empties a word, leaving only its outer letters

parts.note: the first and last letters only
a son is a boy child

explanation.surface: A fighter beats the stuffing out of a teddy boy, a 1950s youth in Edwardian dress.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Teddy boy' reads as one phrase, but splits into two pieces. Teddy boys were 1950s British youths in Edwardian-style suits.
explanation.definitionFit: Mike Tyson is a former world heavyweight boxing champion, so he is an example of a boxer.

clue.text: Luger pistol at the front modified with a silencer

indicators.note: modified means altered, so these letters are changed into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: the front of a word is its first letter, which alone is kept

parts.note: the first letter of the word
taken as written

explanation.surface: A Luger handgun is adapted at the muzzle to take a silencer.
explanation.walkthrough: A Luger is a German pistol; 'silencer' wants to be a gun part, but it is something that silences the ear.
explanation.definitionFit: An earplug is pushed into the ear to block out noise, making things quiet for the wearer.

clue.text: Reason I pass; lecturer reflecting on college

indicators.note: a reflection shows things back to front, so the pieces before it are read in the other direction

parts.note: taken as written
to pass a turn is a go; pass and go both mean move along
L is the standard abbreviation for lecturer
C is the standard abbreviation for college

explanation.surface: A student explains passing thanks to a tutor's thoughts on college.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down entry 'on' puts the reversed group above the last letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Logic and reason both mean sound, orderly thinking that leads to conclusions.

clue.text: Son getting punched, not hard, is floored

parts.note: S is the standard abbreviation for son

indicators.note: not means without, so the letter for the next word is taken away

parts.note: a punched person has been thumped
H is the abbreviation for hard, as on pencils

explanation.surface: A boy takes a punch, a soft one, and is still knocked down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Floored' looks like knocked down, but it means baffled.
explanation.definitionFit: To be floored by a question is to be baffled, unable to answer it.

clue.text: Old-fashioned piano, on property, missing foot

indicators.note: the foot of a down entry is its bottom, so the last letter of the word is dropped

parts.note: p is the musical abbreviation for piano, meaning softly
an asset is an item of property

explanation.surface: An outdated piano stands on a property, one of its feet gone.
explanation.definitionFit: Passé, from French for past, describes something no longer in fashion.

clue.text: Naked old woman in apartment

indicators.note: one piece placed in another is held within it

parts.note: a flat is the British word for an apartment
gran is short for grandmother

explanation.surface: An elderly woman is found unclothed in her flat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Naked' suggests undressed, but it is the sense of open and undisguised, as in naked greed.
explanation.definitionFit: Naked ambition is flagrant ambition: both words mean shamelessly obvious.

clue.text: Underwear, without padding, so plain

indicators.note: padding fills the middle, so taking it out leaves only the outside letters

parts.note: a bra is underwear; its outer letters are kept
sic is Latin for so or thus

explanation.surface: An unpadded bra is a very plain piece of underwear.
explanation.walkthrough: The padding is the bra's middle letter; sic is printed in quotes to mean the original was written so.
explanation.definitionFit: Basic and plain both mean simple, without frills or extras.

clue.text: Notice member bending rules

parts.note: M is the abbreviation for member, as in MP
arching is bending into a curve
orders are rules or commands

explanation.surface: A club member is told off for bending the rules.
explanation.walkthrough: Marching orders are a dismissal: to be given them is to be sacked or sent away.
explanation.definitionFit: Being given notice means being told your job is ending, the same as being given marching orders.
